syllabus_topics: Introduction to Thermodynamics and basic concepts

Closed and open systems. Properties. Concepts of state and equilibrium, processes and cycles. Units: nomenclature, International System, unit conversion. Mass and moles. Volume and density. Pressure. Temperature, Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics.
Properties of pure substances and ideal gas model

Pure substance. Phases of a pure substance. Phase change process. Property diagrams in phase change processes. Property tables. The ideal gas model: ideal gas equation of state, specific heats, internal energy, enthalpy and specific heats using the ideal gas model. Models of solids and liquids.
Work: mechanical systems, thermodynamic systems, boundary work, dissipative work. First Law. Internal energy. Heat. Energy balance in closed systems.

Transition from control mass to control volume. Conservation of mass. Conservation of energy. Analysis of steady-state equipment: nozzles and diffusers; throttling devices; turbines, pumps and compressors; heat exchangers. Transient analysis.

Introduction to the second law. Reversibility. Concept of reservoir, power machine, efficiencies, reverse cycles: refrigerators and heat pumps. Statements of the second law. Consequences of the second law: Carnot corollaries, thermodynamic temperature scale, Carnot power cycle and reversed Carnot cycle.

Concept of entropy. The principle of entropy increase. Entropy variation in pure substances. Isentropic processes. Property diagrams that include entropy. TdS relations. Entropy variation in solids and liquids. Entropy variation using the ideal gas model. Reversible work in steady-state control volumes. How to minimize the power consumed by a compressor? Isentropic efficiencies. Entropy balance.

Basic considerations in cycle analysis. Brayton cycle. Rankine cycle. How to improve efficiency? Reheat cycles. Open regenerators and closed heaters. Reverse cycle: refrigerators, air conditioning and heat pumps.
Mixtures of gases and vapors. Properties of humid air. Characteristic temperatures. Psychrometric diagram. Processes with humid air.
teaching_methods: Personal interview with the course instructor
Student study based on different information sources
assessment_rules: To pass the course, a minimum grade of 4 out of 10 is required on the final exam, and 5 out of 10 on the weighted sum of all grades. If the minimum final exam grade is not met, the global final grade will be the final exam grade. For the extraordinary call, students can choose between two methods: either the ordinary call percentages where the final exam counts 70%, or the final exam counts 100% cancelling partial grades. The student must communicate their choice in writing before the exam, otherwise the first option applies.
